# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# The postcard header layout is DESIGN.md §5b's; nothing here was captured from a run.
# Expectation for the doctor check `history_cache_fresh` (DESIGN.md §7.1) against input/history.bin.
# How to read this file: tests/fixtures/doctor/node_layout/expect.json.
#
# SEAM: FMONERO_CACHE_DIR is already a documented Paths override (§5b, Paths::discover), so the harness
# copies input/history.bin into a temp cache dir and points FMONERO_CACHE_DIR at it. No new seam needed.
#
# input/history.bin IS A HEADER ONLY -- 30 BYTES, NO BODY -- AND THAT IS DELIBERATE.
# §5b's CacheHeader is { magic b"FMHX", format_version u32, wallet_fp [u8;16], high_water u64,
# built_at i64 } and this check reads it through history::header(ctx), which is documented to return
# Ok(None) for an absent file and never to load rows. The BODY is a postcard-encoded Vec<Transfer>, and
# Transfer is Phase 1a's struct: postcard is NOT SELF-DESCRIBING (which is exactly why the header carries
# format_version at all, §3.1), so Phase 0 cannot encode a body that will still decode after Phase 1a
# finalises the field order. A header-only file is the honest fixture for a header-only check.
# CONSEQUENCE, STATED SO IT IS NOT DISCOVERED LATER: this file is NOT a loadable cache.
# history::load(ctx, account) on it must fail or return nothing, and a test that expects rows from it is
# testing the wrong thing. §5b's rule covers that case too -- "a header mismatch is STALE, not corrupt:
# ignored and refetched, never an error" -- so a truncated body must degrade the same way.
#
# THE 30 BYTES, so the file can be regenerated and so a decoder can be checked by hand:
#   46 4d 48 58                                      magic b"FMHX", 4 raw bytes, no length prefix
#                                                    (postcard encodes [u8; N] as N bytes)
#   01                                               format_version 1 as a postcard varint
#   23 f3 01 b6 68 27 33 44 a8 53 df 1c 04 00 9f 7b  wallet_fp, 16 raw bytes = the first 16 bytes of
#                                                    sha256(primary_address), where primary_address is
#                                                    wallet/get_address.json's `address`. §5b: the
#                                                    fingerprint only has to notice that this is A
#                                                    DIFFERENT WALLET, it is not resisting an adversary,
#                                                    and the address it hashes is PUBLIC (§2b) -- so no
#                                                    secret is in this file.
#   f8 90 d8 01                                      high_water 3541112 as a varint
#   80 93 d4 aa 0d                                   built_at 1789560000 as a ZIGZAG varint
#                                                    (postcard encodes i64 zigzag: 2*n for n >= 0, so
#                                                    3579120000)
#
# WHY high_water IS 3541112 AND NOT 3541122: §5b caps the cache at
# `height <= wallet_height - CRYPTONOTE_DEFAULT_TX_SPENDABLE_AGE (10)` (src/cryptonote_config.h:49) and
# says "high_water is THAT height, never the tip". The wallet height is 3541122
# (wallet/get_height.json), so 3541112 is the highest legal value. A fixture at 3541122 would encode a
# cache holding rows too young to cache -- rows whose `locked` could still flip.
# status `pass`: §7.1's condition is magic/version/fingerprint match AND the high-water height within
# 1 000 of the wallet's. 3541122 - 3541112 = 10.
# severity `info`, class D, `fixable` false -- all from §7.1's row, and the class is the interesting one:
# §7 walks through why this check is NOT fixable and concludes that a `RemoveFile` Action, with the
# backup, hash pair, recorded inverse, undo path and fixture it would need, buys only the ability to undo
# deleting a file the next `wallet history` regenerates. Removing the only candidate removed the whole
# exception, so THE DOCTOR CANNOT DELETE ANYTHING AT ALL -- a leaner design and a stronger safety claim.
# §7.1's fix_cmd is a runnable hint, `fmonero wallet history --limit 1   # rebuilds the snapshot`.
# EDITED BY THE PHASE 2 DOCTOR AGENT (DESIGN.md §8 hands this directory to it): see
# decisions/phase2-doctor.md for the reason, stated case by case.
# ADDED `_probe.wallet_height` and `_probe.wallet_primary_address`, both taken from
# tests/fixtures/wallet/{get_height,get_address}.json -- the same two files this case's own
# notes already compute against. §7.1's condition is "the high-water height is within 1 000 of
# THE WALLET'S" and the fingerprint is sha256(primary_address)[..16], so neither half can be
# decided from input/history.bin alone; with no wallet the check honestly answers
# skip:no_wallet_height.
# input/history.bin GREW ONE BYTE, from 30 to 31: a trailing 0x00. §5b's snapshot is ONE
# postcard struct -- the header fields followed by `accounts: BTreeMap<u32, Vec<Transfer>>` --
# and postcard encodes a map as a length varint then its entries, so a 30-byte file ends
# before that length and `history::header` (which decodes the whole struct and reports
# `magic_ok: false` on any failure) could not read the header at all. 0x00 is the empty map,
# which keeps the file header-only in substance -- no Transfer bytes, whose layout is Phase
# 1a's -- while making it the decodable snapshot the check reads.
# v5.6 (2026-09-19, DECISIONS V10): `detail_contains` follows the §2o rewrite of this check's
# details. The verdict, severity, class and fixability are unchanged — only the words are, which
# is the whole point of the round: block numbers are grouped the way the rest of the program
# prints them (`3 541 112`, §2o rule 9) and the word "magic" was an implementation detail of the
# file header rather than something a person can act on. §2o.3: these expectations are UPDATED,
# never deleted.
